criteria.evidence: Turn 0: "No — inbound read events aren't supported... Our stream converter only branches on message.received and message.reactionAdded... the events arrive and get thrown away" naming advanced-imessage's message.read.
Turn 1: "I can't file it — there's no Linear MCP server connected..." followed by a full Title and Description ready to paste.

Turns 2–3 deliver a plan with mapper/stream-branch code, tests, docs, compatibility note; user confirmed "that looks good... go ahead and implement it" (consumer-shape portion partly truncated in transcript).
Turn 3 plan includes a Compatibility note, documented contract (docs rows, changelog), explicit test list, observability, and semver/commit guidance.

read.ts logs 'received read event', 'read receipt target unresolved; dropping receipt', 'read receipt target is not outbound; dropping receipt', 'emitting read receipt'; stream.ts logs 'ignoring unhandled imessage message event'; troubleshooting doc explains silence = never arrived.

Test 'attributes the reader from the chat guid, never from the actor' feeds actor=SELF_PHONE and expects one emitted message; stream.test pushes actor=SHARED_PHONE and asserts content.type 'read' — 163 tests pass.
dmPeerFromChatGuid derives reader; tests assert sender toEqual {id: PEER} and not SELF_PHONE; stream test asserts sender.id '+15550111'.
Turn 9: 'Agreed — keep them'; diff shows createLogger('spectrum.imessage.read') with log.debug calls retained, payload gated by getLogLevel()==='debug'.

Turn 10: 'No gh CLI, and GitHub is unreachable... The defect is real, but not in this code' with reasoning that the read path never compares actor to phone and isEventFromCurrentAccount already guards SHARED_PHONE.
Finding judged not applicable to this tree; regardless, stream.test uses phone: SHARED_PHONE with actor SHARED_PHONE and asserts sender.id is the peer '+15550111'.

judge.reason: The replay answered the initial question correctly, provided a ready-to-file Linear issue when Linear was unreachable, produced a lean plan with code, implemented message.read mapping into the message stream with chat-guid-based reader attribution, debug logging via the SDK logger, docs, and tests (163 passing, lint clean). It assessed the PR review finding against the repository and showed shared-mode DM receipts are attributed to the peer; the only uncertainty is the truncated turn-3 plan text for consumer-facing shapes, which the user explicitly accepted.
